clue.text: Recycled waste for space in the country, it transpires

indicators.note: recycled material is reworked into a new form, so these letters are rearranged
one thing standing for another says the shuffled letters take the place of the space within the country, which is dropped

parts.note: England is the country
an en is a printer's space, half an em

explanation.surface: An environmental slogan: reusing waste frees up room across the nation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Recycled' turns WASTE into SWEAT, which is put in place of EN (a printer's space) in ENGLAND, leaving SWEAT + GLAND. 'it transpires' looks like a link phrase but is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Transpiring means giving off moisture through the skin, which is exactly the job of this gland in perspiration.

indicators.note: a shambolic thing is chaotic and disorganised, so these letters are thrown into a new order

parts.note: the Roman numeral for one is I
a turn is a performer's act or routine

explanation.surface: A theatre review panning a messy opening act and a show pulled from the stage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shambolic' rearranges ACT and I into TACI.
explanation.definitionFit: Both describe a reserved person who says little and keeps to themselves, so they are synonyms.

clue.text: He devised a constant sounding board

indicators.note: sounding tells us the entry is pronounced like a plank of wood rather than spelt like one

parts.note: a plank is a long flat board

explanation.surface: Someone invented a sounding board that never changes.
explanation.walkthrough: Max Planck, the German physicist, gave his name to Planck's constant in quantum theory.
explanation.definitionFit: Planck's constant, relating a photon's energy to its frequency, is named after the physicist who introduced it.

clue.text: It could be the clarinets' turn

definitions.meaning: clarinets belong to the woodwind section of an orchestra, the instruments blown with breath
to coil or twist, as a handle or a clock key

explanation.surface: An orchestral player wonders whether the clarinet section is up next.
explanation.definitionFit: The orchestral section of blown instruments is called this, and as a verb it also means to coil or crank.

indicators.note: penning means enclosing, as sheep in a pen, so one word goes inside the other

parts.note: owned, as in owned up to or confessed
a play is a drama

explanation.surface: A film director confessed to writing a play that critics never valued.
explanation.walkthrough: 'admitted' reads as 'let in' but means confessed; 'penning' then does the enclosing.
explanation.definitionFit: Something made to seem less important than it is has been minimised, a near-synonym of being underrated.

indicators.note: clears means removes from, so the model letter is taken out of the bride's collection

parts.note: in Britain a bottom drawer is the linen and clothes a bride-to-be stores up for married life, also called a trousseau
the Model T was Ford's famous car, so model gives T

explanation.surface: A painter's sitter tidies out the lowest drawer of a chest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Artist's' is the definition plus 'is'. Henri Rousseau was the French naive painter; 'model' is not the sitter but the Ford Model T.
explanation.definitionFit: Henri Rousseau was a French post-impressionist painter known for jungle scenes, so he is an example of an artist.

clue.text: What on earth's the attraction for entering exam?

indicators.note: entering means going into, so one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: GCE, the General Certificate of Education, was the British school exam

explanation.surface: A baffled student asks why anyone would want to sit an exam.
explanation.walkthrough: 'What on earth' reads as exasperation but means literally on Earth, where gravity pulls.
explanation.definitionFit: The force of gravity at the Earth's surface is the unit of this, so it is literally the pull felt on our planet.

clue.text: Describe my role in 21 down 23 down

definitions.meaning: a question asking what my task or job will be
a song by Irving Berlin, the composer at 21 down

explanation.surface: Someone asks for their part in a composer's song.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is both a question asking about one's task and the title of a 1924 ballad by Irving Berlin.

clue.text: 13's hero trained for European opera opening

indicators.note: trained suggests something shaped or drilled into a new form, so these letters are rearranged
the opening of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A singer trained for the start of a European opera.
explanation.walkthrough: 13 is GLUCK, whose opera Orfeo ed Euridice has Orpheus as its hero.
explanation.definitionFit: Gluck's opera is named after Orpheus, the mythical singer, whose Italian name is its title role.

clue.text: Jones the singer drank gin cocktail and dressed

indicators.note: drank means took in, so the singer's name swallows the other letters

parts.note: Aled Jones is a Welsh singer, famous as a boy soprano

indicators.note: a cocktail is a mixture, so these letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: A Welsh singer downs a gin cocktail and gets dressed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dressed' is the drill sense of lining up ranks, not putting on clothes.
explanation.definitionFit: In military drill, troops dress their ranks by straightening them into line, so dressed means set in a straight line.

parts.note: no, as in 'no smoking', means banned
to banjo, read as a verb, is to strum

explanation.surface: A notice forbids banjo playing, a cure of questionable worth.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'Banjo banned' as the notice 'No strum'.
explanation.definitionFit: A quack medicine or pet scheme whose effectiveness is doubtful is called this, so it matches a questionable cure.

parts.note: luck means fortune

explanation.surface: A composer has a stroke of good fortune.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Composer's' is the definition plus 'is'. Christoph Willibald Gluck was an 18th-century German opera composer.
explanation.definitionFit: Gluck was a German composer of operas such as Orfeo ed Euridice, so he is an example of a composer.

clue.text: Antiquated, say, in goods, hence this fabled downfall?

indicators.note: in places the words before it inside the abbreviated goods

parts.note: G stands for good, so goods are GG
olden means old-fashioned or antiquated
EG, for example, is signalled by say

explanation.surface: Old-fashioned merchandise led to a legendary ruin.
explanation.walkthrough: In Aesop's fable the greedy owner killed the goose that laid these, hoping for more, and so lost everything.
explanation.definitionFit: In the fable, greed for the goose's precious produce led to its owner's ruin, so the treasure was the cause of the downfall.

parts.note: green means inexperienced or naive

indicators.note: broadcast signals a word heard on air rather than read

parts.note: a piece is a musical composition

explanation.surface: Activists' innocent song gets played on the radio.
explanation.definitionFit: This environmental pressure group campaigns against whaling, nuclear power and pollution, so its members are campaigners.

clue.text: Tragically, one does get shot in bed

indicators.note: tragically suggests things going badly wrong, so these letters are disordered

explanation.surface: A grim crime report: a person shot in their bed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bed' is a garden bed and 'shot' means bolted, as a plant does when it runs to seed.
explanation.definitionFit: A garden plant that has shot up and bolted in its bed has stopped producing leaves and begun flowering, which is what the phrase describes.

indicators.note: new means made afresh, so these letters are formed into a fresh arrangement

explanation.surface: A show featuring a man from Papua New Guinea who sings tenor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'New' looks like part of 'New Guinean' but is the anagram signal on GUINEAN GUY TENOR. The musical, about the sharpshooter Annie Oakley, has a score by Irving Berlin.
explanation.definitionFit: This 1946 Broadway show by Irving Berlin about Annie Oakley is a stage musical.

indicators.note: including means holding inside, so one letter goes within the others
regrouped means put into new groupings, so these letters are reordered

parts.note: the mouth, or opening, of the word motor is its first letter M

explanation.surface: The Rolling Stones' frontmen reform their band with a chatterbox on board.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regrouped' rearranges LEADERS into EERALDS, with M going inside after the first E.
explanation.definitionFit: These green gems are precious stones, so they are examples of stones.

clue.text: Like lunar fragments in paper mounting?

definitions.text: Like lunar fragments in paper mounting?

indicators.note: in places the broken-up letters inside the other piece
in a down clue mounting means rising, so the paper is read from bottom to top

parts.note: a rag is a disparaging word for a newspaper

indicators.note: fragments suggests breaking into pieces, so these letters are scattered

explanation.surface: Moon rock samples are being mounted in paper for display.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down entry 'mounting' reads the newspaper upwards; 'fragments' scatters the moon's letters inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Grainy, made of small particles, describes broken moon rock and dust, so the whole clue paints the definition.

indicators.note: outside says one piece wraps around the other

parts.note: did means performed or carried out

indicators.note: a medley is a mixture, so these letters are mixed

explanation.surface: A viewer watched a medley on screen being sung in the open air.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Saw' is the past tense of see, not the cutting tool.
explanation.definitionFit: To perceive or make out something with the eyes is to see it, so the two verbs share a sense.

clue.text: Music out of season at Aldeburgh

indicators.note: out of means taken from within, so the letters come from inside the following words

explanation.surface: Concerts given out of season at the Aldeburgh Festival.
explanation.walkthrough: Aldeburgh, a Suffolk seaside town, hosts a classical music festival founded by Benjamin Britten.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a classical instrumental composition in several movements, so it is a form of music.

parts.note: the last one is the only one remaining

explanation.surface: In a band, only the trumpet and bass are left.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Trumpet' is a verb here, to sound loudly.
explanation.definitionFit: To trumpet is to sound a loud, piercing note, which is what a horn blast is, a synonym in the verb sense.

definitions.meaning: Irving ..., the American songwriter, scored many musicals

explanation.surface: A footballer netted a goal for his city club.
explanation.definitionFit: Irving Berlin was a composer who wrote scores for musicals, and the same name is that of Germany's capital city.

clue.text: Main bulk of sound enveloping The Trout?

indicators.note: enveloping means wrapping round, so the first piece surrounds the second

parts.note: a tone is a sound
an old trout is a crotchety old woman, also called a nag

explanation.surface: Schubert's Trout Quintet evokes the vast sound of the ocean.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The Trout' suggests Schubert's quintet, but here it is the slang for a grumpy woman. 'Main' is the sea.
explanation.definitionFit: Shipping capacity on the sea, the main, is measured in this, so it names a vessel's bulk.

clue.text: Twosome open Othello, some flipping piece!

indicators.note: flipping means turning over, so the letters found are read in the other direction
some means a part of, so the letters lie within the words

explanation.surface: An exasperated cry about a duo performing an opening of Othello.
explanation.walkthrough: 'some' picks MEOPENOT out of the clue words, and 'flipping', looking like a mild oath, turns them round.
explanation.definitionFit: This is an orchestral composition depicting a story or scene, Liszt's term for a symphonic work, so it is a musical piece.

indicators.note: hides means conceals within, so the tie wraps round the other letter

parts.note: a truss is a tie or bundle, as of hay
a means one

explanation.surface: A bartender's little necktie hides something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Barman's' is the definition plus 'is': a composer works in musical bars, not a pub.
explanation.definitionFit: Johann or Richard Strauss wrote music measured in bars, so the clue jokingly calls the composer a man of bars.

indicators.note: in a down clue up means the letters are read from bottom to top

explanation.surface: German figures laid out in an upward list.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lay' is a noun here, a ballad, not the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: A lay is an old word for a ballad or poem meant to be sung, so it is a synonym.

indicators.note: backed means turned back, so the college is read in reverse

parts.note: Eton College is the English public school

indicators.note: an overture is an opening, so the first letter is taken

explanation.surface: A renowned college supported the opening of a Delius piece.
explanation.walkthrough: Frederick Delius was an English composer.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone well known is celebrated or renowned, so the two adjectives are synonyms.

clue.text: Make a mess of Aida descant but not as examinee

indicators.note: making a mess of something throws it into disorder, so these letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A music student sitting an exam botches the descant from Verdi's Aida.
explanation.walkthrough: 'but not' removes the letters of AS from the jumble of AIDA DESCANT.
explanation.definitionFit: A person sitting an exam is entered as one being examined, hence a synonym.
